reason: Dropped again: the bank episode cannot be sourced, and Akinlade's own accounts point the other way. In the Y Combinator podcast transcript (ycombinator.com/blog, October 2018) he says banks in Nigeria 'started reaching out to me to help them build software', that he built software for about three banks, and that this gave him access and an understanding of the financial system. Paystack's own blog post of its 2015 YC application (paystack.com, 11 September 2017, with Akinlade's commentary) shows that before YC it had already 'partnered with Access Bank', with a university friend handling the banking-partnership paperwork, and that the bank had asked it to onboard its merchant customers. Pages read that load: the YC application post, the YC podcast transcript, Mixergy's interview transcript (2020), TechCabal (4 September 2017 podcast notes and 25 November 2020 profile, both now load), IFC 'The Maker' (December 2020), Nairametrics (2018, 2021) and Deeds Magazine; none describes Nigerian banks refusing or stalling the start-up. Indie Hackers #072 returns 403. A different, well-sourced pre-YC episode exists if an editor wants it: in 2015 Akinlade, applying to YC as a solo founder after a friend emailed YC partners without his knowledge, had $1,300 in revenue, 12 pilot merchants and about 400 on a waiting list, and pilot merchants used Paystack before any settlement system existed, leaving money with it for over six weeks (YC application post; YC podcast; Mixergy; TechCabal 2020). Not written here because the brief for this retry was the bank episode. Editor note: Paystack suspended co-founder Ezra Olubi in November 2025 over sexual misconduct allegations (Nairametrics, 14 November 2025); search results also show later headlines about his appointment being terminated, which were not read. Any future Paystack edition should be considered with that in mind. Source conflicts seen: founding year 2015 (Paystack, Deeds) vs 2016 (IFC); Akinlade says he first applied to the YC Fellowship in August and was rejected before the October application; Stripe price 'more than $200 million' (IFC, TechCabal) vs EUR 180m (Irish Independent headline, per the earlier retry note).
